source: Research Key Question 5 (Hebrew4Christians 'Similar Letters' rules, Mezzoguild, Hebrewversity, Wikipedia: Cursive Hebrew). Hints paraphrase those rules.

sets.hint: Bet's base sticks out to the right past the back; kaf is a single curved stroke like a reversed c; pe has a curl inside.
Gimel has a foot at the bottom left; nun has a flat base and no foot.
Dalet has a sharp corner and its top bar sticks out past the stem; resh is one rounded curve; final kaf is a resh with a long tail.
Vav is a plain single stroke; zayin has a bar that sticks out to the right at the top; final nun is an extra-long vav that drops below the line; yod is short and floats at the top.
He has a gap (window) at the upper left; chet is closed; tav has a foot that points left.
Samekh is rounded; final mem is square.
Tsadi's second stroke comes from the top right; ayin's second stroke comes from the top left.
Final pe curls inward at the top left; final tsadi forks upward like a Y.
Shin has its dot on the upper right (sh); sin has its dot on the upper left (s). Dots are often left off in handwriting.

cursiveExtra.hint: Rapid cursive dalet and resh look alike; dalet leans and is angled.
Final kaf and qof transformed alike in cursive; qof has a descender at the left.
Shin's central stroke was lengthened like tsadi's right arm.
